subject.title: Vertex beta INVALID_ARGUMENT can wedge long sessions without actionable recovery

question: Should generic LiteLLM/Vertex beta 400 `INVALID_ARGUMENT` be recovered through a provider-owned classifier, a broader session circuit breaker, or left to existing context/media recovery work?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the safe recovery semantics depend on maintainer intent because generic invalid-argument can mean several incompatible provider failure classes.

options.title: Provider-owned classifier and recovery
options.body: Add a narrow LiteLLM/Vertex hook-backed classifier for the proven error shape and require focused live or realistic provider proof before merging.

options.title: Generic invalid-argument circuit breaker
options.body: Treat repeated generic provider 400s as a session recovery problem across providers, accepting a broader compatibility and misclassification review surface.

options.title: Defer to neighboring recovery work
options.body: Keep this distinct issue open only as tracking context while related context-overflow or media-rejection work lands, and close it later if those paths prove sufficient.

recommendation.title: Provider-owned classifier and recovery
recommendation.body: Add a narrow LiteLLM/Vertex hook-backed classifier for the proven error shape and require focused live or realistic provider proof before merging.

likelyOwner.reason: The provider-hook and structured failover history points to steipete as the strongest available owner for the product boundary decision.
